references.text: The direct opposite of verse 26: Here those described as 'my sheep' are defined as those who hear his voice and follow him, while verse 26 defines unbelievers as not belonging to him.

A parallel logic where belonging to God determines the ability to hear and believe God's word: 'The one who is from God hears the words of God; therefore you do not hear, because you are not from God'.
Jesus' prayer in which he distinguishes between the disciples given to him ('those who are yours') and the world emphasizes that belonging to him is a given reality that sets them apart from others.
John uses the same criterion to distinguish between God's children and the devil's children: 'Whoever does not practice righteousness is not of God, nor is he who does not love his brother'.
The prophecy that the Lord himself will shepherd his sheep and they shall be his people, an image Jesus picks up and makes concrete when he speaks of 'my sheep'.
